title: Reddit Will Go Logged-In Only as AI Search Cuts Its Traffic
dek: AI summaries mean fewer clicks, so Reddit wants everyone to sign in.

facts.label: Weekly search referrals lost in October
Q3 2026 revenue, up 53% year over year
US daily users lost in one quarter

caption:
The days of reading Reddit without an account may be numbered. 👀

Reddit says it is moving toward a logged-in only experience, with first tests in select markets outside the US before the end of the year. The reason: AI search. Google's AI summaries and answer engines now answer questions directly, so far fewer people click through to Reddit threads. Search referrals fell by more than 1 million per week in October, and US daily users dropped from 53.2 million to 50.7 million in a single quarter.

CEO Steve Huffman calls it a big change, but the business case is clear: logged-in users mean sharper ad targeting, tougher protection against AI companies scraping its archive for free, and more leverage in data licensing deals. Revenue is still booming at $895 million for Q3, up 53%.

We're tracking this at AI Parabellum because it's one of the clearest signs yet of how AI is reshaping the open web. Would you make an account just to read Reddit?

post_caption:
AI ate the search clicks, so Reddit is putting up a wall.

The platform plans to require accounts for most browsing, starting with tests outside the US this quarter. Fewer drive-by visitors, more ad signals, and less free data for AI scrapers. Expect other big content sites to watch closely.
